name: global_budget_concentration_near_clifford_angle_snapping
precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz; 2 <= qubits <= 20. Requires at least one non-Clifford rz whose angle theta satisfies v4.api.angles.rz_distance(theta - nearest multiple of pi/4) <= the error the rule draws from the shared pool (5e-4), i.e. at least one angle within sin^-1(2*5e-4) of the pi/4 grid. On qae_13 the angle histogram contains the near-Clifford family -pi/2 + pi/2^k (-1.57002934, -1.56926235, -1.56772837, -1.5646604, -1.55852448, -1.54625263), whose first member is 7.67e-4 = pi/4096 away from -pi/2, so rz_distance = sin(3.83e-4) = 3.83e-4 < 5e-4 and the trigger matches there; circuits with no angle inside the whole pool are excluded and cost nothing.
identity: Rz(theta) = Rz(theta*) * Rz(theta - theta*) with theta* the nearest k*pi/4. If theta* is a multiple of pi/2 the factor Rz(theta*) is the Clifford z/s/sdg (0 T of synthesis), if it is an odd multiple of pi/4 it is t/tdg (1 T, no synthesis); the residual Rz(theta-theta*) is DROPPED and its phase-aligned operator distance |sin((theta-theta*)/2)| is charged to the ledger. The procedure is the allocator, not the snap: collect every rotation i of the whole circuit with cost_i = rz_distance(theta_i - theta_i*) and gain_i = the T that gridsynth stops paying for it (gain_i = T(eps_rz) if theta_i* is a pi/2 multiple, T(eps_rz) - 1 if it is an odd pi/4 multiple), sort by gain_i/cost_i, and greedily accept while sum of accepted cost_i <= the amount drawn, re-pricing after each accept because deleting one rotation lowers N_Rz and therefore RAISES eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz for every survivor, which lowers every survivor's cost by 3*log2(N_Rz/(N_Rz-1)) and can bring a second candidate inside the remaining pool. The whole 5e-4 pool is spent on the single globally best few rotations rather than divided between blocks.
correctness: Exact algebra: Rz is a one-parameter group, so the split Rz(theta) = Rz(theta*)Rz(theta-theta*) is an identity, and Rz(k*pi/2) in {z,s,sdg} and Rz(+-pi/4) in {t,tdg} are exactly representable (v4.api.dv.with_ops performs exactly this lowering). The only error is the deleted residual, a one-rotation window whose phase-aligned operator distance the judge measures as exactly |sin(delta/2)| = v4.api.angles.rz_distance(delta); distances of independent accepted snaps add in the worst case (diagonal phase errors on independent basis bits do not cancel in the operator norm, so the sum is the honest bound and is what is drawn). No qubits, no measurement, no Clifford frame change beyond a diagonal gate replacing a diagonal gate, so commutation with everything downstream is unchanged and the whole-circuit check against the ORIGINAL circuit sees only the drawn error. Each accepted application is individually verified, so a mis-priced candidate is rejected, not silently kept.
trigger: Over the op list after the book: for every op with v4.api.dv.is_rotation and not v4.api.dv.on_grid(angle), compute theta* = the nearest multiple of pi/4 (v4.api.angles.dyadic(theta, 2)) and cost = v4.api.angles.rz_distance(theta - theta*). Emit matches only for rotations with cost <= v4.api.budget.remaining(), ordered by (T saved)/cost descending; emit them one at a time so the runner prices and verifies each before the next is offered, and stop when budget.draw(cost) refuses. Rotations already on the pi/4 grid, and rotations whose distance exceeds the pool, are not matched.
expected_effect: On qae_13 exactly one rotation is affordable: the angle -1.57002934 = -pi/2 + pi/4096 snaps to -pi/2 = sdg for 3.83e-4 of the pool, turning one of the 88 synthesized rotations into a free Clifford. That removes its gridsynth sequence (~51 T at eps_rz = 1.136e-5, from (4526 - 14 explicit T)/88 = 51.3 T per rotation) and drops N_Rz from 88 to 87, which raises eps_rz for the 87 survivors and shaves 3*log2(88/87) = 0.05 T off each, ~4 T more. Second-order: with eps_rz relaxed, no further angle comes inside the 1.17e-4 left, so the allocator stops. The point of difference against the floor's DPF rule is allocation, not snapping: DPF splits the 5e-4 into equal per-block shares over ~20 width-4 blocks, giving each block ~2.5e-5 - an order of magnitude less than the 3.83e-4 this one snap needs - so DPF provably cannot buy it (fingerprint fixable_at_k['2'] = 0 at the per-rotation eps_rz threshold, but 76 at k=14, i.e. the circuit has exactly one angle that a concentrated budget can move onto the pi/4 grid). Expected final T ~4471, inside the 151 T of angle_cost headroom and honestly short of DPF's 4264.
source: Ross & Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations' (arXiv:1403.2975) for the 3*log2(1/eps) cost law that makes gain/cost the right greedy key; Gheorghiu, Mosca & Mukhopadhyay, 'T-count and T-depth of any multi-qubit unitary' / Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca on exact pi/4-multiple representability; the non-uniform precision-allocation argument of Campbell, 'Shorter gate sequences by mixing unitaries' (PRA 95, 042306) and of Bocharov-Roetteler-Svore on budgeting synthesis error across many rotations rather than splitting it uniformly.
